title: London was flooded by beer

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1814, a wave of beer killed eight Londoners.
beats.visual: Brown frothy wave sweeps down a sketched London street toward camera

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: October 1814, Horse Shoe Brewery, central London.
beats.visual: PD c.1800 view of the Horse Shoe Brewery; sketch map pin at Tottenham Court Road

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How does beer flood a street?
beats.visual: Ava icon; beer glass tips over

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: A vat 22 feet tall held about a million pints of porter. But there was a problem. It burst.
beats.visual: Giant wooden vat with height ruler '22 ft'; counter '1,000,000 pints'; hoops snap

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where did all that beer go?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Into St Giles, a packed slum. A 15-foot wave knocked down walls and flooded basements.
beats.visual: PD 1852 'A Scene in St Giles's' engraving; wave crashes through; basement windows fill brown

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Nobody. Eight died, including mourners at a wake. A jury called it an act of God.
beats.visual: Eight small candles light up; jury bench sketch; stamp 'ACT OF GOD'

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The brewery got its tax back. The Dominion Theatre stands there now.
beats.visual: Coins slide back to a brewery ledger; sketch of the Dominion Theatre facade

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Eight lives, lost to beer. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Foam settles; History Sketches corner logo

description: On 17 October 1814 a huge vat of porter burst at the Horse Shoe Brewery in London, sending a wave of beer through the St Giles slum and killing eight people. A jury called it an act of God. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #london #strangehistory
